name: Pekahiah (son of Menahem)
title: Israel's short-lived king
summary: Pekahiah was the seventeenth king of the northern kingdom of Israel and reigned for only two years. He followed in his father Menahem’s sinful footsteps by worshiping the golden calves. He was killed in a coup led by his own officer Pekah, who then took the throne.

keyEvents.title: Becomes king over Israel
keyEvents.description: Pekahiah became king of Israel in Samaria after his father Menahem’s death, in the fiftieth year of King Azariah’s reign over Judah.

keyEvents.title: Continues in sin
keyEvents.description: Pekahiah did what was evil in the Lord’s sight. He did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, which had caused Israel to sin.

keyEvents.title: Murdered by Pekah
keyEvents.description: His own officer, Pekah son of Remaliah, conspired against him and killed him in the royal palace at Samaria, along with Argob and Arieh and fifty men from Gilead.

keyEvents.title: Pekah Takes the Throne
keyEvents.description: After the murder of Pekahiah, Pekah became king in his place. This marked the end of Menahem's dynasty after only one generation.
